text: This is Drawer on the Mac. The spec lives on the left, the drawing in the middle, and the inspector on the right.
Start from an example. Here's a C4 container diagram for an internet bank, written in PlantUML.
Select anything in the drawing, and its line lights up in the spec. Drag it, and only the layout changes. The spec stays clean.
Type in the spec, with completion for macros, names and arrows, and the drawing follows as you type.
Or just sketch. Draw a box, tell Drawer what it is, give it a name, and draw a line to connect it.
Your voice works too. Add a database called ledger, then connect payments to it.
One click converts the whole diagram between PlantUML and Mermaid. And PNG or SVG exports keep the editable diagram inside.
Auto layout tidies it up. Drawer. Sketch it, or write it. It stays in sync.
